title: Versioned migrations
description: Write the change into migration files, hash and check them, then apply them in order.
note: Direct apply and versioned migrations are different ways of working, not two halves of one. schema apply writes nothing into migrations/, and migrations up never reads schema.sql. A project picks one.

files.schema.sql:
-- The schema you want the database to have.
--
-- Ptah reads this file as the desired state, reads the real catalog out of
-- app.db, and works out the difference. You never write ALTER statements here.

CREATE TABLE users (
  id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name  TEXT NOT NULL,
  email TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE tasks (
  id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  title   TEXT NOT NULL,
  done    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users (id)
);
files.README.md:
# Workspace

    schema.sql   the schema you want
    app.db       an empty SQLite database
    migrations/  written by ptah migrations generate

This is the other route. Scenario A applies a plan straight to the database.
Here Ptah writes the plan into files you review, commit and replay in order.

    ptah migrations plan     --schema-file schema.sql --db-url sqlite://app.db
    ptah migrations generate --schema-file schema.sql --db-url sqlite://app.db \
                             --migrations-dir migrations --name init
    ptah migrations hash     --dir migrations
    ptah migrations validate --dir migrations
    ptah migrations lint     --dir migrations --dialect sqlite
    ptah migrations status   --migrations-dir migrations --db-url sqlite://app.db
    ptah migrations up       --migrations-dir migrations --db-url sqlite://app.db

The flag is --dir on the verbs that only read the directory, and
--migrations-dir on the verbs that also talk to a database. That is the CLI's
own spelling, not a typo here.

seed:
-- Scenario C starts from an empty database. The migrations build it.
PRAGMA user_version = 0;

baseline.message: This route reads schema.sql out of the workspace, and it is not there. The steps below no longer describe what you have. Everything still works; Reset puts the scenario back.

steps.title: Plan
steps.caption: See the SQL first
steps.headline: See the SQL before it becomes a file.
steps.instruction: app.db is empty. plan prints the statements that would close the gap, with a safety classification per statement, and writes nothing.
steps.done: Two CREATE TABLE statements, both classified safe. Still nothing on disk and nothing in the database.

steps.title: Generate
steps.caption: Write the files
steps.headline: The plan becomes something you can review and commit.
steps.instruction: Same difference, written to disk this time: an up file and a down file, named with a version prefix. Note that this verb spells the flag --migrations-dir.
steps.done: The migration is a file now. It can be read in review and replayed on another database.

steps.title: Hash
steps.caption: Lock the directory
steps.headline: Hashing stops history being rewritten quietly.
steps.instruction: hash writes migrations/ptah.sum. Anyone editing an already-shipped migration afterwards will fail validation instead of quietly changing history. This verb spells the flag --dir.
steps.done: ptah.sum is in the workspace. Commit it alongside the migrations.

steps.title: Check
steps.caption: Validate and lint
steps.headline: The two checks you would run in CI.
steps.instruction: validate compares the directory with ptah.sum. Without a sum file it exits 2 and tells you to run hash. lint reads the statements and reports what it thinks is risky.
steps.done: The directory matches its sum and lint found nothing. Both are checks you would run in CI.

steps.title: Apply them
steps.caption: In order, once each
steps.headline: Applied in order, recorded, and never applied twice.
steps.instruction: up applies every pending migration in version order and records what it applied in schema_migrations. Run status before and after to see the version move.
steps.done: users and tasks exist, and schema_migrations records the version that created them. Running up again applies nothing.

finished.headline: Two routes to the same desired state.
finished.caption: schema apply changes the database now; migrations up replays a reviewed history. A project picks one, and Ptah does both.
